title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a case-by-case construction of a canonical Riemannian metric on each conformal surface X, orientable or not, whose analytification falls among the exceptional, non-hyperbolic uniformization types. The goal is to show that X carries a metric, canonical up to the stated normalization, that depends only on the conformal structure and is preserved by every conformal automorphism, holomorphic or antiholomorphic. This is presumably groundwork for the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes', where every surface should carry a canonical metric (hyperbolic in the generic case).

(i) Case X ≅ C*. The flat metric |dz|/|z| is canonical up to a positive scalar. Grothendieck fixes the scalar by requiring the circle |z|=1 to have length 1, which gives |dz|/(2π|z|). The margin identifies this as the push-forward of the unit Euclidean metric dz dz̄ on C under z ↦ exp(2iπz), C → C*. The same recipe defines the metric on every X ≅ C*.
- The holomorphic automorphisms z ↦ az (|a|=1) and z ↦ a/z preserve it.
- So does the antiholomorphic map z ↦ z̄.
- Hence every conformal automorphism preserves the canonical metric.

(ii) Non-oriented case: X ≅ real projective plane minus one point, i.e. the open Möbius band of that conformal type. Its orientation double cover X^or is ≅ C*, with deck involution of the form z ↦ −1/z̄. That involution is an isometry, so the canonical flat metric descends to X and is again invariant under all conformal automorphisms.

(iii) Case X ≅ E_C, the complex affine line, i.e. X^an ≅ C. On a complex line L, the Riemannian metrics compatible with Hermitian structures are all proportional.
- They are not invariant under all affine automorphisms. They are invariant only under the subgroup generated by translations and multiplications by unimodular u ∈ U = {|z|=1}.
- They are, however, quasi-invariant (rescaled by a constant) under arbitrary automorphisms, which are affine.
- The next page concludes that on X ≅ E_C one gets translation-invariant flat metrics, canonical only up to R+*. They are determined by the conformal structure (X has a canonical complex affine line structure), but no normalization is possible because the area is infinite.

The following page treats RP^2 via the antipodal involution on P^1_C, and then P^1_C itself.
errors: Minor: in the E_C case the transcription reads 'par contre invariantes par automorphismes quelconques', which contradicts the preceding sentence. The manuscript almost certainly says 'quasi-invariantes', i.e. invariant up to a scalar factor. With that reading the argument is correct.
Section numbering: the case labelled '2°)' should be 2'') (a sub-case following 2'), consistent with the surrounding numbering 2', 3, 3'.
No mathematical errors. The normalization |dz|/(2π|z|) matches the push-forward via exp(2iπz). The descent to RP^2 minus a point is valid because z ↦ −1/z̄ is an isometry of |dz|/|z|.

ideas.what: Canonical flat metric on C* normalized so the unit circle has length 1, obtained as the push-forward of the Euclidean metric via exp(2πiz), and invariant under all holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Flat cylinder metric / uniformization of the punctured plane

ideas.what: Descent of canonical metrics from the orientation double cover to non-orientable conformal surfaces (Klein surfaces), here the open Möbius band RP^2 minus a point
ideas.modern_name: Dianalytic / Klein surfaces; uniformization of non-orientable surfaces via the orientation cover
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses non-orientable surfaces and the Teichmüller tower including them, but not this metric normalization

ideas.what: On the complex affine line, Hermitian-compatible metrics are invariant only under translations and unitary rotations and quasi-invariant under all affine automorphisms, so there is a canonical metric only up to R+*
ideas.modern_name: Euclidean similarity structure on C; non-normalizable flat metric (parabolic type)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but entirely classical bookkeeping of canonical metrics for the exceptional uniformization types (C*, Möbius band, C), including the non-orientable ones. It is useful context for Grothendieck's conformal-surgery project, but it contains nothing beyond standard uniformization theory.
transcription_corrections: Top-left '4)' is the folio/page number of the section, not a mathematical item.
Line 2: something crossed out before '1' (looks like 'zz' or '2π'), then 'soit 1'.
'de [?] = façon [?]' should read 'de même façon' (written '= façon').
'∀ automorphisme [?] conforme respecte la mesure canonique' is better read as 'tout automorphisme conforme respecte la métrique canonique'.
'2°) Cas X ≃ E_C' should be '2'') Cas X ≃ E_C'.
'Les métriques riemanniennes sur une droite vectorielle' likely reads 'sur une droite vectorielle complexe L', with 'déf. par les' as an interlinear insertion.
'elles sont par contre invariantes par automorphismes quelconques' should read 'quasi-invariantes par automorphismes quelconques'.
Margin: 'déduite de l'unité' is likely 'déduite de la métrique conforme zz̄ sur C via z ↦ exp 2iπz, de C sur C*'.
